body.x: At CES 2026, Montreal-based deep-tech firm CubicSpace Technologies officially bridged the gap between professional spatial capture and everyday mobile viewing. The company unveiled CubicScreen, a hardware-and-software solution that transforms standard iPhones into glasses-free 3D displays, earning a prestigious “Impact Award (third place)” at the Global Innovation Forum 2026.

Since Apple introduced spatial video capture in 2023, millions of users have been recording memories in 3D, yet most have been forced to view them in 2D or invest in expensive headsets like the Apple Vision Pro. CubicSpace CEO and co-founder Nicholas Routhier aims to change that. During a demonstration at the Seoul Pavilion, Routhier explained that the company is bringing 3D into everyday life by enabling users to view 3D images directly on their iPhones in both portrait and landscape modes, without requiring additional accessories.

The product suite consists of two primary components designed to make 3D as intuitive as traditional photography. The first is a thin optical 3D screen protector that overlays the iPhone screen, serving as a specialized glasses-free display. The second is an intuitive application powered by adaptive stereoscopic geometry. Unlike traditional 3D, which uses “one-size-fits-all” settings, this AI-driven model dynamically adjusts 3D depth in real-time based on the specific content and the individual viewer’s conditions. This scientific breakthrough is backed by a robust intellectual property portfolio, including nine granted patents and nine others pending worldwide.

body.cap: CubicSpace CEO Nicholas Routhier (right) during an interview at the Seoul Pavilion with AVING reporter Jay Marcus Kennedy (left) | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The launch aligns with a broader industry shift toward glasses-free immersion. Routhier highlighted this trend by citing developments such as Samsung’s Odyssey 3D monitor and the rise of 3D Gaussian Splatting, a technology that converts single photos into navigable 3D environments. CubicSpace’s impact was validated at the Global Innovation Forum, an international startup competition hosted by the Seoul Business Agency (SBA) at Eureka Park. Competing against representative startups from seven leading tech nations—including Switzerland, Israel, Japan, and France—CubicSpace was awarded the Impact Award and a cash prize, selected by a panel of global media outlets and venture capital firms.

With a commercial release targeted for Q2 2026, CubicSpace is currently using the CES platform to secure global distributors and explore software integration with other VR headset and 3D display manufacturers. The company is also eyeing the growing VR 180 entertainment market in South Korea as a key area for expansion, positioning smartphones as the primary entry point to the expanding spatial media ecosystem.
